# Step 1: Name a drink for the house menu

## Why naming?

Three drinks are already on the menu: Mona Latte, Copilot Cortado, and Ducky Cold Brew. They are worked examples, not competition entries. They are never scored and never appear on the leaderboard.

Your job is to invent a fourth that has never been served here. This is one five-minute exercise, and everything happens on the counter screen. There is no terminal, no GitHub sign-in, no pull request, and nothing to install.

## Start your order

Choose Start my order. The station mints a barista handle for you, in the style of a generated workspace name. Keep it: it is how your entry is identified on the house menu and the leaderboard, and how you find your place later.

The handle is generated at the counter and is unique within this event's menu. It is not a GitHub account and it is not tied to your identity.

## Pick your mascot and where it sits

Every drink must carry one mascot: mona, ducky, or copilot. The mascot may sit anywhere in the name, not only at the front. Monsoon Mona Cold Brew and Ducky's Last Stand are as valid as Mona Moonrise.

The mascot picker and the placement picker are optional. Leave them alone and the station reads the mascot straight from what you typed. Set them and they become a claim the station checks against your name, so a disagreement is reported back to you rather than silently corrected. Placement earns no points; choose the position you like best.

## Invent the name

Type your drink name and choose Add it to the menu. A bare mascot on its own is rejected, because Mona or Ducky alone would let the first attendee permanently claim a name nobody invented. Add something of your own to it.

The menu is first come, first served. If someone has already used your name, the station says so and you try another. Names are compared after normalizing case, spacing, and punctuation, so Mona Moonrise and mona-moonrise are the same drink.

## Read your score

A rubric scores the name out of 5,000 and shows you the breakdown: base credit, alliteration, craft, wordplay, how well it fits the house style, and invention. The rubric is deterministic. The same name always earns the same score, and no model generates your feedback or your score.

A mid-range score is a normal result. Most invented names land well below the maximum, because every category has to be earned.

## Take your place and hand over

Your drink joins the house menu and the leaderboard for the rest of the event. Equal scores share a rank.

When a leaderboard destination is configured, the station shows a scannable code and a link to your place on it. If no destination is configured, no code is shown; nothing is invented to fill the space.

Choose I'm done - hand over to the next barista. That clears the counter for the next person. Your drink stays on the menu and your entry stays on the leaderboard; only the station is reset.

## If something goes wrong

If the screen loses its connection, choose Refresh connection. The station reads its saved state rather than inventing a new one, so a reconnect does not cost you your handle, your drink, or your score.

Ask booth staff for help with anything else. You never need to leave this screen.
